info.description: Central English documentation for authentication, support, telemetry and every registered application. Documentation is public. Operation permissions remain enforced. All contracts and explanatory content are owned by api_for_apps. Source discovery never fetches downstream OpenAPI documents. Backends receive x-display-name only when account identity is attached and a first or last name exists. The value joins nonblank stored first and last names with one space and percent-encodes their UTF-8 bytes. Decode once with a UTF-8 percent decoder, not a form decoder. Client-sent copies are removed on all proxy routes. No route or setting is added.

get.description: Non-consuming browser continuation preview. Supply only the opaque handoff_id query parameter and an allowed Origin (configured auth-app origin or a registered bound-target origin), and include credentials. Returns data.account (email),current_account (email or null),account_mismatch,target_app,study_id,browser_state,expires_at. It returns no session credentials or source content. It sets a host-only HttpOnly browser_handoff cookie and, when absent, the shared readable csrf cookie. Keep browser_state in browser memory; never place it in a URL. For redeem/cancel send that state in JSON and csrf in X-CSRF-Token, retaining cookies and the same Origin. A second preview in the same cookie store rotates the state without extending the continuation expiry. Another cookie store cannot claim an existing binding. An existing different browser account requires explicit user confirmation before redemption. Expired,used,cancelled or revoked-source continuations refuse. Responses prohibit caching and referrer propagation. No polling is required.

200.description: Preview and binding created; include credentials and retain browser_state for redeem/cancel.

400.description: Invalid continuation.

401.description: Source installed-app session is no longer valid.

403.description: Origin or browser binding refused, or native handoff disabled.

post.description: Redeem a short-lived authentication artifact issued by this gateway. Send the registered application Origin header. The artifact can be redeemed once and must belong to that application. A successful response sets the HttpOnly sid session cookie and the readable csrf cookie. Browser clients must include credentials on later gateway calls. Mutable session requests send the csrf cookie value in X-CSRF-Token. Production cookies share the Asodya domain and use Secure when reached through HTTPS. This operation returns no user data. Installed-app branch: when handoff_id is present the body is {"app", "handoff_id", "secret"} and no Origin header is needed. The gateway checks that the handoff exists, its status is done and the login is less than 5 minutes old, SHA256(secret) equals the challenge (constant-time), app matches, and the app network equals the browser network at login (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /64). It then marks the handoff used, keeps the record for 30 minutes and returns {"session_id", "csrf_token", "expires_in"} without cookies. The app stores both values in OS secure storage and sends Cookie: sid=<session_id>; csrf=<csrf_token>, plus X-CSRF-Token on changes; POST /user/sync/v1/log-out ends only that device session. Native sessions renew a 30 day idle limit on each use and end 90 days after creation. Answers (data.code): HANDOFF_NOT_FINISHED 409 (no record yet: finish the login in the browser), HANDOFF_EXPIRED 410 (login older than 5 minutes; the status stays expired), LOGIN_REFUSED_NETWORK 403 (correct secret and app, but the app network differs from the browser network at login; message "Login refused. The login came from a different location."; only the first such finish gets this answer, the handoff is then used and kept), HANDOFF_USED 409 (already used outside the retry window, wrong secret, wrong app, or any finish after a network refusal; the handoff cannot be used again), INVALID_HANDOFF 400, NATIVE_HANDOFF_DISABLED 403, RATE_LIMITED 429 (IP limits as for log-in). Retry: for 2 minutes after a successful finish the same handoff_id, secret and network return the same session, only while that session still exists. NATIVE_HANDOFF_ENABLED=false turns the installed-app path off, including existing native sessions. Browser continuation uses explicit action modes on this same route. create_browser_handoff requires a valid native sid session with its csrf cookie and X-CSRF-Token; JSON has only action,target_app=certifications,study_id. It binds the trusted source user/session, purpose and opaque study reference. The auth_apps continuation page first uses GET on this route with only handoff_id. Browser Origin must be the configured auth-app origin or a registered origin of the bound target app. Redeem/cancel also match the exact preview Origin, browser cookie, browser_state, csrf cookie and X-CSRF-Token, and the browser session seen at preview. patch.description: Sign in through the gateway using email and password, or an authenticated provider access token supplied by the Auth flow. The response data is a short-lived opaque exchange artifact, not a session cookie or a user profile. Pass that artifact to the registered application exchange endpoint. The optional app identifies the initiating application and defaults to certifications. Email and IP limits apply, with progressive delay for repeated attempts. Invalid credentials return 401. Installed apps (handoff mode): send the optional handoff_id, challenge and platform with app. handoff_id and challenge are base64url without padding of 32 bytes; challenge is base64url(SHA256(the 32 raw secret bytes)); the secret never leaves the device. platform must be listed for app in NATIVE_APP_PLATFORMS (annotations: linux, macos, android, ios, ipados; cortex: android, cli). After the normal user check the gateway stores the handoff (one login per handoff_id, valid 5 minutes) with the browser IP and network and answers "Login complete. Return to the app." with data {"expires_at": <unix seconds>} and no exchange artifact. Errors carry data.code: INVALID_HANDOFF (400), NATIVE_HANDOFF_DISABLED (403), HANDOFF_USED (409, handoff_id already used). Without handoff_id the response is unchanged.
